clue.text: Fixes up crack in middle of desk

indicators.note: in says the joke sits inside the letters picked from the desk
middle of takes the central letters of the word desk, dropping its ends

parts.note: a crack is a witty remark, a quip

explanation.surface: Someone repairs a split running down the centre of a writing desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' looks like a split in the wood, but it is a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip something is to fit it out with what it needs, which is fixing it up.

clue.text: First in election, Prime Minister assuming he has long time — but such things are transitory!

indicators.note: first in picks the opening letter of the word election
assuming means taking on, so the leader's abbreviation takes in the pronoun

parts.note: an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A newly elected leader thinks he has years ahead, but such power is fleeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemera are items of short-lived interest or use, things that do not last.

clue.text: Not like sliced bread, this burns crust regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter from the words burns and crust

explanation.surface: A whole loaf whose crust is scorched evenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second, fourth and every alternate letter of 'burns crust'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sliced bread has been cut; a loaf left whole is uncut.

clue.text: Job on wharf ultimately insufficient for researcher

parts.note: a post is a job

indicators.note: ultimately insufficient means the word falls short at its end, losing its last letter

parts.note: a dock is a wharf

explanation.surface: A dock-worker's job doesn't pay enough for a scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately insufficient' cuts the final K from DOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: A postdoc is a researcher who has completed a doctorate and holds a postdoctoral post.

clue.text: Tighten your belt and behind — adults are going to be slender

indicators.note: are going says the adults depart, so those letters leave the combined words

parts.note: to tighten your belt is to economise, to save
behind in time means late
A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult, so adults is two As

explanation.surface: Diet advice: cinch your waist and your bottom, and grown-ups will become slim.
explanation.walkthrough: SAVE + LATE gives SAVELATE; 'are going' takes away its two As to leave SVELTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Svelte describes a figure that is slim and graceful, a synonym of slender.

clue.text: Queen entering royal museum gallery

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the queen's letters go into the museum's

parts.note: the V and A, the Victoria and Albert Museum in London, named after the royal couple
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The monarch walks into a gallery of a royal museum.
explanation.walkthrough: The V and A is London's Victoria and Albert Museum, written V AND A. 'Gallery' looks like part of the museum, but it is the porch.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallery can be a roofed, open-sided walkway along a building, which is a veranda.

clue.text: Zany lass running round you, talking — one circulates with food

indicators.note: round means the scrambled letters go around the next piece
running suggests the letters of zany lass are set in motion and rearranged
talking means the word you is taken by its spoken sound

parts.note: you is said aloud as the letter U

explanation.surface: A wacky girl dashes around you, chattering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' gives LAZYSSAN, and 'round' wraps it around the letter U, which sounds like 'you' when 'talking'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy Susan is a revolving tray on a dining table, turning dishes round to diners.

clue.text: Cake from leavened grain with half fat stuffing

indicators.note: stuffing says the half-portion of fat is filled inside the rearranged grain
leavened means raised and transformed, so the grain's letters are rearranged

parts.note: rice is a grain

indicators.note: half means only the front portion of the word for fat is used

parts.note: lard is a cooking fat

explanation.surface: A bake made from raised grain stuffed with reduced-fat filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leavened' rearranges the grain to ECIR, an indirect anagram of a synonym rather than of a clue word.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a small cream-filled pastry, a kind of cake.

clue.text: Stocky peasants taking part in Asian festival

indicators.note: taking part in places the country folk within the festival's letters

parts.note: Tet is the Vietnamese lunar new year festival
hicks are unsophisticated country people, peasants

explanation.surface: Sturdy farm workers join in the celebrations of an Asian festival.
explanation.walkthrough: Tet is the Vietnamese new year.
explanation.definitionFit: A thickset person is heavily built and solid, which is what stocky means.

clue.text: Influencer to advertise jacket

parts.note: to trail a film or show is to advertise it in advance
a blazer is a jacket

explanation.surface: A social-media figure promotes a jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Influencer' suggests social media; here it means a pioneer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trailblazer is a pioneer whose new ideas shape others, an influencer in the older sense.

clue.text: Junket of raspberry with rind of lime

parts.note: a raspberry is a rude noise, also called a razz

indicators.note: rind of means the outside letters of the word lime, its first and last

explanation.surface: A dessert of raspberry flavoured with lime peel, junket being a milk pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junket' looks like the dessert of the surface, but here it means a spree. 'rind of' gives LE, the outer letters of lime.
explanation.definitionFit: A razzle is a lively spree or binge, and a junket is a pleasure trip or jaunt.

clue.text: Midriffs rejected as obscene content

indicators.note: rejected means the word for the bellies is thrown back, read in reverse

parts.note: tums are tummies, the midriff area

explanation.surface: Images of bare bellies are censored as indecent material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns TUMS round.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is indecent or pornographic material, obscene content.

clue.text: Working out problem, I had backtracked, lacking certainty

indicators.note: backtracked means the contracted form of I had runs backwards

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd, written ID
an agnostic holds that certainty about God is impossible

explanation.surface: Someone retreats in doubt while trying to solve a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backtracked' turns the contraction I'd round; an agnostic is a person without certainty about God.
explanation.definitionFit: Diagnostic describes the process of identifying what is wrong, working out the problem.

clue.text: Finding fault with service — that's liable to produce a reaction

definitions.text: that's liable to produce a reaction

parts.note: critical means finding fault
mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A complaint about a church service is likely to provoke a response.
explanation.walkthrough: The reaction is a nuclear chain reaction, not a churchgoer's response.
explanation.definitionFit: Critical mass is the minimum amount of fissile material needed to sustain a nuclear chain reaction.

clue.text: They perform sensationally in oral assessments

definitions.text: They perform sensationally in oral assessments

parts.words: They perform sensationally in oral assessments
parts.note: sensationally means through the senses: these organs in the mouth judge flavours

explanation.definitionFit: Taste buds are the sensory organs on the tongue that judge flavour, assessing what enters the mouth.

clue.text: Greek islander having no right to catch fabulous sea creature

indicators.note: to catch means the shortened islander's word holds the next piece inside
having no means the islander's word goes without the letter for right

parts.note: a Cretan is a native of Crete
ace means excellent, fabulous

explanation.surface: A Greek with no rights manages to land a mythical sea monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no' leaves CETAN, and 'to catch' takes the excellent piece inside. 'fabulous' looks like part of a mythical beast, but means excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A cetacean is a whale, dolphin or porpoise, a marine mammal.

clue.text: Not part of match, cared about having only one goal

parts.note: something not part of a matching pair is single, unpaired
minded means cared about, as in 'I wouldn't have minded'

explanation.surface: A footballer left out of the game but bothered about scoring just once.
explanation.walkthrough: The football 'match' and 'goal' are misdirection: the match is a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-minded person pursues one aim with determination, having only one goal.

clue.text: Absence of nap, having start of afternoon off, is most curious

indicators.note: off means that letter is removed from the phrase

parts.note: no siesta means an absence of a nap

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of the word afternoon

explanation.surface: Skipping your afternoon snooze makes you most inquisitive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes A, from 'start of afternoon', taking the last A from NO SIESTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosiest is the superlative of nosy, meaning most inquisitive or prying.

clue.text: Messi's header getting kid excited about minute when Champions League opponents meet?

indicators.note: header means the first letter, the head of the word Messi's
about means the stirred-up letters go around the next piece
excited suggests the letters of kid are stirred up and rearranged

parts.note: minute, meaning tiny, is wee

explanation.surface: A football star heads the ball, and a youngster gets excited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' gives IDK. Champions League games are played on Tuesdays and Wednesdays.
explanation.definitionFit: Champions League football matches are played on Tuesday and Wednesday evenings, in the middle of the week.

clue.text: Queen embracing old flame in outbuilding

indicators.note: embracing means holding the former partner within the queen's name

parts.note: Anne was Queen of Great Britain, 1702-1714
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: A queen hugs her former lover in a shed.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is a building added to or near a main building, an outbuilding.

clue.text: Lacking height, failed to prepare wall adequately?

definitions.meaning: too small, short of the usual height
size is a gluey sealant brushed on walls before papering

explanation.definitionFit: Undersized means smaller than normal; read as under-sized it means given too little size, the wall sealant.

clue.text: Defect following piece of legislation

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
a law is a piece of legislation

explanation.surface: A shortcoming that results from a new statute.
explanation.definitionFit: A flaw is a fault or imperfection, a synonym of defect.

clue.text: Rifle shot gets you bit of a promotion

indicators.note: shot means broken or ruined, so the letters of rifle are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rifle shot gets a mention in an advertising campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like firing the rifle, but it is the rearranging signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A flier is a leaflet handed out as one piece of an advertising campaign.

clue.text: Judge's case gets thirty days, showing lack of experience

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, here the first and last letters of Judge

parts.note: June is a month of thirty days

explanation.surface: A judge's ruling gets thirty days in jail, revealing naivety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' takes JE, the outer letters of Judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Jejune means naive and simplistic, showing a lack of experience or maturity.

clue.text: Freshly cut grass roughly tied

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

indicators.note: roughly says the letters of tied are put together in a rough, rearranged way

explanation.surface: Newly mown grass is bundled up carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freshly cut' looks like mowing; it means edited again. 'roughly' rearranges TIED into ITED.
explanation.definitionFit: A film or text re-edited has been cut and revised once more.

clue.text: Fake keepers at zoo houses

indicators.note: houses says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Animal enclosures supposedly look after zoo creatures, but are counterfeit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an inferior substitute or imitation, something fake.

clue.text: Star grabbing drink — this is liable to go downhill!

definitions.text: this is liable to go downhill!

indicators.note: grabbing says the star holds the drink within it

parts.note: the sun is a star
kir is a drink of white wine and cassis

explanation.surface: A celebrity snatches a drink, heading for a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go downhill' suggests decline; the slope is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski run is a slope or course that skiers descend, so it literally goes downhill.
